title: Sequoia: Scalable, Robust, and Hardware-aware Speculative Decoding
technique: DP-optimized speculation tree topology, sampling-without-replacement verification robust across temperatures, hardware-aware tree size/depth selection

optimized_metrics.evidence: how can we design an optimal tree-based speculative decoding method to maximize speedups on modern hardware?

we formulate tree construction as a constrained optimization problem and employ a dynamic programming algorithm to discover the optimal tree [maximizing expected number of tokens generated per verification, G(n,d)]
speculative decoding to accelerate LLM inference while preserving the LLM's output distribution

headline_claim.text: SEQUOIA improves the decoding speed of Llama2-7B, Llama2-13B, and Vicuna-33B on an A100 GPU by up to 4.04x, 3.73x, and 2.27x. To serve Llama3-70B-Instruct on a single L40 GPU through offloading, SEQUOIA reduces the per-token decoding latency to 0.60 s/token, 9.5x faster than DeepSpeed-Zero-Inference.

reported_metrics.where: Tables 1-4 speedup and TBT ms/token; offloading s/token
Tables 1-2 generated tokens per step in parentheses; Fig 4

metric_definitions.definition_quote: TBT refers to time between tokens.
metric_definitions.notes: Here TBT is the mean wall-clock per-token latency of a single sequence at batch 1 (ms/token, includes speculation overhead), i.e. total decode time / tokens, not the per-token gap distribution of a serving system

metric_definitions.definition_quote: the speedup attained by SEQUOIA can be expressed as Speedup(n,d) = G(n,d) / (t(n)+d*c) [t(n)= time for target to verify n tokens / time to verify 1 token; c = draft time per token / verify time]
metric_definitions.notes: hardware-aware model of speedup relative to incremental decoding (24.2 ms/token HF on A100)

metric_definitions.term_as_written: number of generated tokens per decoding step
metric_definitions.definition_quote: We specify the average number of generated tokens per decoding step in parentheses, next to the speedup factor.

load_regime: batch=1 (small-batch and offloading regimes; 'The optimal tree also depends on the batch size, which can be considered by the hardware-aware optimizer' but not evaluated); 128-token prompt and generation
tradeoff_acknowledged: Optimal tree depends on acceptance-rate vector (draft/target pair, temperature, domain) and on batch size; per-setting measurement is work-intensive. Larger trees trade verification cost vs accepted tokens.
hardware: A100-PCIE 80GB, L40 (on-device); L40 with CPU offloading (Llama3-70B)
models: Llama2-7B/13B, Vicuna-33B, Llama2-70B, Llama3-70B-Instruct; drafts JF68M, Llama2-7B-chat, Llama3-8B
workloads: C4(en), OpenWebText, CNN DailyMail, MT Bench; 200 eval examples (50 offloading)
extractor_notes: Note TBT used for single-stream per-token latency. Speedup is vs HuggingFace incremental decoding. Offloading 0.60 s/token vs DeepSpeed-Zero-Inference 5.7 s/token.
